pairs.why: B runs the truss off-frame like the real card and keeps the background to a soft light-ray gradient, while A adds an invented floating truss with yellow end caps.
Both put the chair on a plain peach ledge against a red-orange gradient, so staging and detail don't separate them.
Both use the same flat sunburst field with the hero floating, differing only in hue.
Both use a quiet tone-on-tone wavy purple pattern with similar load and no competing props.
B adds invented props (stacked cans, striped ball, flag) and a busy brick wall, while A keeps a calmer shelf with only the bear and target, closer to the real card's few large shapes.
B's sunburst has a glowing yellow center like the real card, while A's rays are flatter and more orange, but both are simple fields.
A has a quiet backdrop of a few large dune and sky shapes, while B adds many small bushes, rocks, ties and mesas that make the environment busier than the real cards.
B has fewer posts, a calmer sea and larger quiet shapes, while A has many posts, dense water caustics and a wide, busy scene unlike the real tight close-up.
